findings.explanation: resolvePageCredential() decrypts the Facebook page access token and immediately writes the raw plaintext secret to console.log on every successful resolution, with no redaction. This runs on the hot path for any message/webhook handling that needs a page credential, so the long-lived token ends up in stdout/log aggregators in full. Contrast with core/webhook.js, which consistently passes outbound text through redactSensitiveText()/pageRef() before logging — this file has no equivalent guard. Anyone with log access (or a log-shipping misconfiguration) can extract the live Graph API token and impersonate the page.
